display_name.help: Name users see when creating (e.g. Coding Agent); falls back to the name if blank

description.help: One line on what this environment is good for

engine_kind.help: Choose the program that powers this Environment, such as Claude Code or Codex. Assistant runtimes are used by Assistants and cannot be selected for Agents.

enabled.label: Enabled
enabled.help: When off, this environment is hidden from the user's selectable list

sandbox_backend.label: Sandbox service
sandbox_backend.help: Choose the service that creates and manages this Environment's sandboxes. Leave blank to use the deployment default.

runtime_template_name.label: Sandbox image or template
runtime_template_name.help: Leave blank to use the deployment default for the selected Agent program

type.label: Outbound network access
type.help: Unrestricted permits every outbound destination. Limited permits only the hosts below plus platform-required model, callback, tracing, and declared Plugin repository hosts.

allowed_hosts.label: Additional allowed hosts
allowed_hosts.help: Exact hosts or leftmost wildcards such as *.example.com. Used only in limited mode. Do not include schemes, ports, or paths.

allow_mcp_servers.label: Allow remote MCP servers
allow_mcp_servers.help: In limited mode, also permit the remote MCP endpoints explicitly declared by each Agent. Plugin-internal endpoints are not visible to AstraBox and must be listed above.

idle_action.label: After a conversation is idle
idle_action.help: Choose what happens after the Agent's idle timeout. Terminate deletes the sandbox and its workspace. Pause saves the sandbox filesystem and releases compute; the next message recreates the runtime from those files. Resuming usually takes about ten seconds and requires a snapshot-capable backend. Paused sandboxes are deleted after the deployment's retention period.

sandbox_tenancy.label: Sandbox sharing
sandbox_tenancy.help: Choose whether each conversation gets its own sandbox or conversations using the same Agent share one. Separate sandboxes are the default and provide clearer isolation between users. Shared mode does not safely isolate conversations belonging to users who do not trust one another. It creates a separate Linux user and home directory for each conversation and requires the advanced or privileged sandbox permission level. Assistants use a shared workspace and do not support this setting.

options.agent: Share one sandbox across this Agent's conversations

sandbox_permission_level.label: Sandbox permission level
sandbox_permission_level.help: How much system privilege this Environment's sandboxes are granted. The default level is the minimum, and the one to keep when users do not trust one another: each conversation already has a sandbox to itself, so nothing needs to be separated inside it. The advanced level additionally allows separate areas to be created inside a sandbox, which two things need — conversations that share one sandbox and must be kept apart from each other, and an Agent program that applies its own restrictions inside (Codex enforces its permission mode that way; without this level it asks for consent each time instead of allowing the action). AstraBox asks the selected sandbox provider for the level and verifies the running sandbox before using it. OpenSandbox does not offer privileged because its lifecycle API exposes no privileged-container attestation. A backend only offers levels it can both deliver and prove.

options.default: Default — minimum privilege, for users who do not trust one another
options.advanced: Advanced — separate areas inside a sandbox
options.privileged: Privileged — container as a virtual machine (provider support required)

endpoint_provider.label: Model connection
endpoint_provider.help: Choose a registered model connection for Agents in this environment. Leave blank to use the connection declared as the deployment default.

provider_access.label: Connection details
provider_access.help: Set the model or gateway URL and credential used by every Agent in this environment. Changing it affects all of them.

tracing.label: Agent program tracing
tracing.help: Send the Agent program's own OpenTelemetry spans — the operations it performed, how long each turn took, and where it failed — to a collector you run. This is separate from the deployment's request traces and the model traces recorded by the gateway. An Environment cannot enable tracing when its Agent program does not support it.

enabled.label: Send Agent program spans
enabled.help: Off by default. Turning it off keeps the endpoint and credential, so switching it back on does not mean entering the secret again.

endpoint.label: Collector endpoint
endpoint.help: OTLP/HTTP base URL; the exporter appends the signal path. For Langfuse this is <host>/api/public/otel.

signals.label: Signals
signals.help: Any of traces, metrics, logs. Defaults to traces and metrics, which every OTLP receiver serves — Langfuse accepts no logs. Recording prompts needs logs.

headers.label: Extra headers
headers.help: For a collector that authenticates through its own header rather than Authorization, such as Honeycomb's x-honeycomb-team.

auth_token.label: Authorization header value
auth_token.help: The complete value including its scheme — 'Basic <base64>' for Langfuse, 'Bearer <token>' for most others. Which one is right is the collector's answer, so it is sent exactly as written. Stored write-only: reads show a mask.

auth_token_secret_name.label: Authorization from vault
auth_token_secret_name.help: Name a vault secret instead of entering the value here.

environment.label: Environment tag
environment.help: Recorded on every span as deployment.environment, e.g. production.

log_user_prompt.label: Record prompt text
log_user_prompt.help: Adds what users typed to the exported data. Leave off unless your collector is approved to store it. Requires the logs signal.
